Raontech and SN Display to develop perovskite QD color conversion for OLED microdisplays
content: Korea's Raontech announced that it has signed an MoU with SN Display to co-develop perovskite-based next-generation AR/VR microdisplays. The two companies are already conducting preliminary research in which SN Display's perovskite technology is applied to Raontech's OLED microdisplay samples, in order to verify the performance improvements and potential applications.

title: Samsung supplies over 70% of the OLED panels used by major laptop brands, PC makers turn to Chinese suppliers
content: According to a new report from Chinese market research firm Sigmaintell, Samsung Display supplies more than 70% of the OLED panels used by the major laptop brands. As supply becomes increasingly concentrated, PC makers are starting to approach Chinese OLED makers as alternative suppliers, both to secure panel volumes and to strengthen their bargaining power on prices.

title: Sun Fine Chem clears its IPO listing review, is ready to go public soon
content: In November 2025, we reported that OLED material developer Sun Fine Chem (SFC) is planning to IPO in the Korean stock exchange. SFC, based in Korea, develops materials for OLEDs, organic TFTs, PDP displays and other devices. The company is a subsidiary of Hodogaya Chemic

title: AI server tracker: semiconductor testing and design services rally on compute demand
content: Within AI server tracking data, a clear parallel growth trajectory has emerged between semiconductor testing interface providers and chip design houses. Driven by the surge in artificial intelligence (AI), high-performance computing (HPC), and custom ASIC developments, both sectors demonstrated substantial year-over-year revenue gains as of September 2026.

title: Samsung to break ground on second Texas chip fab in November
content: Samsung Electronics plans to begin construction of its second semiconductor fabrication plant in Taylor, Texas, in November 2026, moving ahead with its US foundry expansion as its first facility prepares to begin operations by the end of the year.

title: Samsung, SK Hynix aim to ease AI memory bottlenecks with zHBM, HBF
content: Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix are developing new memory technologies to address growing bottlenecks in AI systems, with Samsung exploring a design that stacks high-bandwidth memory (HBM) directly above graphics processors and SK Hynix advancing high-bandwidth flash (HBF) to expand memory capacity for AI inference.

title: Samsung's chip and device chiefs head to Tokyo during Lee's visit
content: Five senior Samsung Electronics executives, including the heads of its semiconductor and consumer electronics businesses, reportedly traveled to Tokyo on October 13 while chairman Lee Jae-yong was visiting Japan, bringing together the company's three executive directors and key corporate decision-makers as it expands cooperation with Japanese semiconductor suppliers.

title: Holtek targets higher-value MCU markets with AI server cooling orders set to lift 2027 revenue
content: Taiwan-based microcontroller (MCU) manufacturer Holtek Semiconductor unveiled its 2026 product roadmap on October 15, focusing on four core areas: smart protection, green energy and intelligent control, edge AI computing, and general-purpose applications.
